use_case: AI resume screening and candidate ranking: the ATS AI match add-on parses resumes, scores each applicant 0-100 against the job order, sorts the list, and can send automatic rejections below a set score
vendor_or_model: AI add-on vendor integrated into the ATS (third-party model; training data not disclosed)
source_evidence: EV-005 (add-on settings and disposition history); EV-006 (add-on terms and help documentation); EV-007 (job ads: no notice or accommodation line); EV-017 (ATS subscription payments)
data_categories: Resumes; application answers; work history; location; job order requirements. No SSNs, IDs, or demographic data
human_in_the_loop: Since 2026-07-21 the score only sorts; the owner reviews every applicant who meets the job order minimums and records a reason when passing over a higher score. Automatic rejection was on for two job orders (2026-04-06 to 2026-06-26; 236 applicants) with no human review
applicable_laws: Title VII 703(b) and 703(k) (42 U.S.C. 2000e-2(b), (k)); ADA 42 U.S.C. 12112(b)(6); ADEA 29 U.S.C. 623(b); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) (vendor holds applicant data); NYC Local Law 144 not triggered (no NYC jobs)

use_case: General-purpose consumer AI chatbot used to draft job ads and outreach messages; resumes were pasted in to draft client summaries (about 30, stopped 2026-07-21)
vendor_or_model: Consumer AI chatbot vendor (free account; history and training on until 2026-07-21)
source_evidence: EV-027 (chatbot account settings and history); EV-017 (no payment: free account)
data_categories: Job descriptions and message drafts; previously resumes with names, contact details, and work history
human_in_the_loop: Owner edits every draft; job ads checked against a short fair-wording checklist before posting
applicable_laws: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) (personal data sent to a vendor); Title VII 704(b) (42 U.S.C. 2000e-3(b)) for job ad wording
status: Approved for drafts with no personal data only; history deleted and training turned off by 2026-09-30
